messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Version 23.12.06 && PARDISO
parts:
Version 23.12.06 (testing with R-4.3) now include the new PARDISO-
version-8 libraries, which you can get/buy a license from, at
www.panua.ch The license conditions are beyond our control.

However,

* Windows is not yet supported. the windows binary they provide does not
'work' for us, and a new build using a different compiler(s) has been
requested. if that happens, Windows builds will be updated.

* Fedora39 (and maybe other very 'new' distro's?). You might experience
half speed compared to older versions and recently it started (for me)
to produce internal (in PARIDSO) memory errors. running in serial mode I
think is fine, but that defy the purpose. This bug/regression was
reported some weeks ago.

* It seems to run fine on various Ubuntu installations.

As said before. We're working on an alternative open-source solution,
but this is a lot of work and it take time. We hope in first half of
2024.

H


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Error Segmentation fault
parts:
Hi,
I’m trying to estimate a coregionalization model with the new version 23.12.06 of INLA and Pardiso, but after a while,  I have this error:
 
Segmentation fault
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
Calls: inla -> inla.core.safe
Execution halted
I don't think is a RAM or CPU problem  (the server has 40 CPU core and 377 GB RAM)
R version 4.3.2 (2023-10-31)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Debian GNU/Linux trixie/sid


#Coregionalization model ----

form <-
  y ~ 0 + Intercept.pm25 + Intercept.pm10 +  AOD550  + PM25 + PM10 +  windspeed10m +
  PBLH_HH00 + PBLH_HH12 + pres + tem2 + cumulprec + altitudedem_std + i_surface_std +  d_a1_std   +
  f(s1,
    model = spde,
    group = g1,
    control.group = ctr.g) +
  f(s2,
    model = spde,
    group = g2,
    control.group = ctr.g) +
  f(
    s12,
    copy = "s1",
    group = g12,
    fixed = FALSE,
    hyper = hyper
  ) 


spde <-
  inla.spde2.pcmatern(
    mesh = mesh,
    alpha = 2,
    constr = FALSE,
    prior.range = c(100, 0.8), # P(range < 100 km) = 0.8
    prior.sigma = c(0.8, 0.2) # P(sigma > 0.8) = 0.2
  )

 inla(form, rep('gaussian', 2),
       data=inla.stack.data(stack,spde=spde),
       control.family = list(hyper.eps, hyper.eps),
       verbose=TRUE,
       control.compute = list(cpo=F,waic=F,dic=T,config=TRUE),
       control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 1, prec=0.01,mean.intercept=0),
       control.predictor =list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),compute=T) )->inla.out


The log is attached

Thank you!
Maria Antonietta Reatini
